 No REAL ID? What TSA accepts for Thanksgiving flights from Delaware
 Damon C. Williams, USA Today Network 2026년 11월 4일 수 오후 6:01 UTC 0 Delaware travelers without a REAL ID may already have another credential that will get them through airport security this Thanksgiving.
 The Transportation Security Administration accepts several alternatives to REAL ID, including U.S. passports, passport cards, DHS Trusted Traveler cards such as Global Entry, Department of Defense IDs and permanent resident cards.
 What IDs can you use instead of a REAL ID?
 Travelers with a valid passport or another TSA-approved credential don't need to use TSA ConfirmID or pay its $45 fee. TSA says ConfirmID is intended for travelers who arrive without a REAL ID or another acceptable form of identification. 
 Advertisement
 One important exception: TSA says a temporary driver's license isn't accepted as checkpoint identification.
 So before paying $45 or making a special trip to Delaware DMV, check TSA's current acceptable-ID list. You may already have what you need to fly. This video explains which identification TSA will and won't accept for domestic flights.
 Damon C. Williams is a Philadelphia-based journalist reporting on trending, breaking and service-related topics across the Mid-Atlantic region for the USA Today Network. 
 This article originally appeared on Delaware News Journal: No REAL ID? What TSA accepts for Thanksgiving flights from Delaware
